messages:
maria: Heads up — after the autoscaler pushed new p4 instances in eu-west-2 during the 03:00 maintenance window, we've seen ~12% of nodes fail GPU init and then kubelet evict pods. Symptoms: modprobe/nvidia probe errors and PCIe AER resets.
kevin: seeing same in monitoring — spike in pod restarts and allocation failures. Can you paste dmesg?
maria: paste of the interesting lines:

```
[    5.432123] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[    5.432456] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: firmware: failed to load nvidia/xxx.bin (-2)
[    5.432789] nvidia: probe failed with error -22
[    5.433100] nouveau 0000:3b:00.0: firmware: failed to load nouveau/xxx_firmware (-2)
[    5.433456] pci 0000:3b:00.0: AER: Multiple Corrected error received: id 00e4
[   10.500000] KWorker: stack trace
```

kevin: -22 on probe usually indicates API mismatch. Which kernel version are these nodes on?
maria: These are rolling in with kernel 6.4.12 from our new image (image-builder: gpu-6.4.12). Canary pool did fine but the autoscaler used the same image for new spot capacity.
jun: Canary passed because it used nvidia-driver v535 and DKMS rebuilt on boot. Spot nodes seem to skip the DKMS rebuild step (we added a racey cloud-init script). Suspect module built for 6.3 vs 6.4 ABI.
olivia: We're also seeing NCCL handshake timeouts on nodes that had partial init — that explains slowjob queues failing but not total meltdown.
maria: immediate ask: pause autoscaler rollout to eu-west-2 and mark nodes draining as unschedulable. Can infra team stop new provision?
kevin: pausing now. Also creating a nodeSelector to keep new allocs away from the affected node pool.
jun: mitigation plan I'm proposing:
- disable autoscaler for pool eu-west-2-gpu-spot (done)
- mark current bad nodes cordoned and remove from LB
- run a forced DKMS rebuild + update-initramfs on one problematic host and test (commands below)

```
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y linux-headers-$(uname -r) dkms
sudo dkms autoinstall
sudo update-initramfs -u -k $(uname -r)
reboot
```

jun: if rebuild succeeds, we can roll a lifecycle hook to run DKMS sync on boot for spot nodes.
olivia: longer term: pin driver/kernel matrix in image-builder and make DKMS build part of AMI bake so modules match before first boot. Also add a boot-time healthcheck that fails instance registration if nvidia probe fails.
maria: agree. Also want to track cost impact — autoscaler replaced some reserved capacity with spot during the window; evictions caused retries and increased egress. Can finance give an estimate? @kevin any quick numbers?
kevin: rough numbers: about 48 failed pod restarts, ~3.7 TB additional egress from retries, and one hour of blocked capacity leading to ~0.6k USD of delayed ML jobs (ballpark). I'll open a cost incident ticket.
jun: action items assigned:
- jun: run DKMS rebuild on 3 repro hosts and confirm probe passes (ETA 2h)
- olivia: add probe healthcheck to instance registration (ETA 1 day)
- maria: stop autoscaler until image bake pipeline is updated (done)
- kevin: cost ticket + notify sales/customers if SLA impacted (ETA 30m)
maria: temporary workaround: add taint gpu-init-failed=true:NoSchedule to hosts that show probe failures so scheduler avoids them until fixed. Also adding a prometheus alert for modprobe failures per-host.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-3110 — kernel-module incompatibility causing GPU init failures in eu-west-2; status: investigating.
kevin: noted. Let's not roll 6.4 image to other regions until we have DKMS baked in. Also check if our dedicated customers hit this (they run private images) — ops to notify dedicated-eng.
maria: will loop in dedicated-eng. Any objections to disabling spot autoscaling overnight? we should be conservative.
jun: no objections. I'll also add a preflight that verifies dkms status and nvidia-smi before allowing instance into pool.
olivia: once warm pool rebuilt, we'll canary with a tiny rollout and verify NCCL handshakes and throughput.
maria: thanks all. I'll keep thread updated with repro logs and whether DKMS rebuild fixed probe on the 3 hosts.
kevin: ping when the first rebuilt host is back up so SRE can re-enable limited rollouts. :thumbsup:
